title: First D.C. job with Johnny Ridgely's small band
summary: Dan Andrews, who went to Howard, had urged him to come; within a week Phillips was in Johnny Ridgely's five or six piece band, living on Corcoran Street.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: So, what was going on in D.C. What did you get into when you first got here?
Oh, when I first got here, I didn't know nobody but Dan -- Dan Andrews. See, when the band broke up, he came here. He didn't go nowhere.
While you were up there in Portsmouth, he came to D.C.
He was in D.C. Because see, he went to school at Howard and his wife was from here. So he came here.
So you knew him when you came to town.

Well, he used to tell me to come here, that he could get me a job. You know what I mean? He said you could play around in Washington. And the job we had in Portsmouth folded up, so I came here -- me and Red and Bill and myself, we came here. So I got here, and a guy had a little band, working in... See, in them days, every club had live music. Some cats was playing with a little old band, but they were getting pretty good money.
A guy named Johnny Ridgely. He's not in the book. He was just around here in Washington.
So he had the band that you came to work with.
He had a little... He had five or six pieces. What did he have? Two saxophones, trumpet, piano and drums. That was the first job I had.
So you came to D.C. in February. When did you get that job?
Whereabouts were you staying at that time?
I was staying on Corcoran Street, right down the street from here.
In Northwest. What was that band into and how long did that job last?
